newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Indonesian asylum-seekers riot in Malaysia.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian asylum-seekers riot in Malaysia.

text.p: More than 50 political asylum-seekers from Indonesia's Aceh province rioted at a Malaysian detention camp on Tuesday to protest against deportation, police and witnesses said.
Police said they used minimal force to quell the two-hour riot at the Langkap camp for illegal immigrants in the north Malaysian state of Perak.
Witnesses said tear gas and batons were used.

Police later loaded the inmates on to five trucks that the witnesses said were believed to be heading to Port Klang near Kuala Lumpur, where two Indonesian ships were waiting to take the detainees back.

"They used tear gas. And then the police attacked them (the inmates). All we could hear was their shouts and cries," said Iqlil Tengku Ilias Leube, a Malaysia-based Acehnese businessman who watched the riot outside the camp.
In the first official reaction, the national Bernama news agency quoted a senior policeman as denying that tear gas was fired and as saying that minimal force was used.
"While we wanted to ensure a peaceful transfer, they (the Acehnese immigrants) tried to create an ugly scene," Assistant Commissioner of Police Abang Abdul Wahab Abang Julai was quoted as saying.
"No shots were fired in their direction, no tear gas was used...we tried our best to ensure the transfer goes smoothly," Abang Abdul added.
A Reuters journalist at the camp saw two inmates with their heads bandaged being loaded on to a truck.
As the trucks rolled out of the camp, shouts of "Aceh Merdeka" (Free Aceh) from the inmates were heard.
Free Aceh is a pro-independence movement that has alleged that asylum-seekers deported to Indonesia are murdered.
Hundreds of Acehnese have fled across the Malacca Strait separating Indonesia's Sumatra and Malaysia since March 1992 to escape fighting between the Indonesian army and Free Aceh.

Malaysia has not recognised the Acehnese as political asylum-seekers and says it will send them home. Police spokesman Shamsuddin Ali told Reuters the last deportation of Acehnese was in June this year, when about 20 were sent back.
